1507.subject: Physics
1507.text: The motion of planets in the solar system is an example of the conservation of
1507.sol: One deuteron consists of one proton and one neutron. As the mass of a proton and a neutron is approximately same $\left(\approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}\right)$, we assume that the mass of the neutron be $m$ and the mass of the deuteron be $2 m$ as the electron mass is negligibly small compared to that of proton and neutron. Let the initial velocity of the neutron be $u$. As the deuteron is initially at rest, the final velocity of the neutron is v_1=$\left(\frac{m-2 m}{m+2 m}\right)$u=-$\frac{m u}{3 m}=-\frac{u}{3} .$and the velocity of the deuteron is v_2=$\frac{2 m}{m+2 m}$u=$\frac{2}{3}$u $\text{. }$Total energy before collision is $E_1=\frac{1}{2} m u^2$ After collision, the energy gained by the deuteron is E_d=$\frac{1}{2} \times($2 m) v_2^2=m $\times\left(\frac{2}{3}$u\right)^2=$\frac{4}{9}$m u² . $E_d$ is the amount of energy lost by the neutron. Therefore the fractional loss of energy of the neutron is $\frac{E_d}{E_1}=\frac{(4 / 9) m u^2}{(1 / 2) m u^2}=\frac{8}{9}$

2087.subject: Zoology
2087.text:
Assertion : Corpus luteum is produced by Graafian follicle after ovulation.
Reason : It secretes estrogen which is necessary to maintain pregnancy.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2087.sol: After ovulation, the empty Graafian follicle contains a blood clot which is called corpus haemorrhagic. Its granulosa cells continue to proliferate, develop yellow carotene pigment or lutein and get converted into lutein cells. This converts the ruptured follicle into yellow body called corpus luteum. It becomes a temporary endocrine gland secreting progesterone with small quantity of estrogen. in absence of fertilization, after few days, corpus luteum ultimately stops activity, loses yellow colour, begins to degenerate, then it is called corpus albicans. If fertilization occurs and foetus is implanted in the endometrium, the trophoblast cells of the developing placenta secrete a hormone human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG). This hormone, like LH, maintains the corpus luteum and the secretion of progesterone and estradiol by it. These two hormones check the breakdown of the endometrium of the uterus. Thus corpus luteum helps to maintain pregnancy.

& =\frac{2-x}{2+\frac{3 x}{2}}=\frac{4-2 x}{4+3 x}=\frac{(4-2 x)(4-3 x)}{\left(16-9 x^2\right)} \\
& =\frac{16-20 x+6 x^2}{16-9 x^2}=\frac{16-20 x}{16}\left\{\because x^2 \text{ negligible }\right\} \\

\end{aligned}\)

9575.sol:
We have

\end{array}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
\sin (A-B) & =\sin A \cos B-\cos A \sin B \\
& =x \cdotx-\sqrt{1-x^2} \cdot \sqrt{1-x^2}\\
& =x²-1+x² \\
\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)& =2 x²-1 \\
\Rightarrow 2 x²-1 & =\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow2 x²=\frac{3}{2} \Rightarrowx^2=\frac{3}{4}\\
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}$

10687.text: A bag contains 19 red balls and 19 black balls. Two balls are chosen at a time repeatedly and discarded if they are of the same colour, but if they are different, black ball is discarded and red ball is returned to the bag. The probability that this process will terminate with one red ball is
10687.sol:
3 different cases formed
Case I : When both red balls are chosen, then both balls are removed from the bag.
Case II : When both black balls are chosen, then both balls are again removed from the bag.
Case III : When two different balls are chosen, the red ball is returned to the bag.
The bags in the balls after second last trial will be (red, black) or (red, red, red).
$\therefore$ In both cases, there would be a red ball in the bag, Hence, the probability of red ball in bag is 1.

10713.subject: Mathematics
10713.text: Which of the following is not a property of a Binomial distribution?
options: Random experiment consists of a sequence of $n$ identical trials
Each outcome can be referred to as a success or a failure
The probabilities of the two outcomes can change from one trial to the next
10713.sol:
We know that properties of Binomial Distribution are

  • There are two possible outcomes: true or false, success or failure, yes or no.
  • There is '$n$' number of independent trials or a fixed number of $n$ times repeated trials.
  • The probability of success or failure remains the same for each trial.
  • Only the number of success is calculated out of $n$ independent trials.
  • Every trial is an independent trial, which means the outcome of one trial does not affect the outcome of another trial.

So, the probabilities of the two outcomes can change from one trial to the next is not a property.

13851.text: A bullet of mass $10 \mathrm{ g}$ pierces through a plate $A$ of mass $500 \mathrm{ g}$ and then gets embedded into a second plate $B$ of mass $1.49 \mathrm{ kg}$ as shown in the figure. 13851.sol:
Let $v_1$ be the initial velocity of bullet and $v_2$ be the velocity with which each plate moves.

So, applying law of conservation of momentum,

$\begin{aligned}& m v_1=M_1 v_2+\left(M_2+m\right) v_2 \\
& 0.01 v_1=0.5 v_2+(1.49+0.01) v_2
\end{aligned}
  \\ 
Let $v_3$ be the velocity of bullet, when it comes out of plate $M$.

So, momentum of bullet between plate $M_1 and M_2$ = Sum of momentum of plate $M_2 and $bullet.

\begin{aligned}m v_3 & =\left(M_2+m\right) v_2 \\
0.01 v_3 & =(1.49+0.01) v_2=1.5 v_2
\end{aligned}
  \\ 
\begin{aligned} \% \text{ loss$ in $} \mathrm{KE} & =\frac{(1 / 2) m v_1^2-(1 / 2) m v_3^3}{(1 / 2) m v_1^2} \times 100 \\ & =\frac{v_1^2-v_3^2}{v_1^2} \times 100\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\left\{1-\left(\frac{v_3}{v_1}\right)^2\right\} \times 100 \\ & =\left\{1-\left(\frac{150}{200}\right)^2\right\} \times 100 \\ & =\left(1-\frac{9}{16}\right) \times 100=\frac{7}{16} \times 100=\frac{7}{4} \times 25 \\ & =43.75 \%\end{aligned}$

16341.text:
For a system to follow the law of conservation of linear momentum during a collision, the condition is :
(1) total external force acting on the system is zero.
(2) total external force acting on the system is finite and time of collision is negligible.
(3) total internal force acting on the system is zero.
16341.sol:
From Newton's second law,
$F=\frac{d p}{d t}$
If $F=0$, then $\frac{d p}{d t}=0\Rightarrow \quad p=$ constant
Thus, if total external force acting on the system is zero, then linear momentum of the system remains conserved.

18709.text: Number of solutions of equations $\sin 9 \theta=\sin \theta$ in the interval $[0,2 \pi]$ is
18709.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Given, } \quad \sin 9 \theta=\sin \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin 9 \theta-\sin \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos \left(\frac{9 \theta+\theta}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{9 \theta-\theta}{2}\right)=0 \\
& {\left[\because \sin C-\sin D=2 \cos \left(\frac{C+D}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{C-D}{2}\right)\right]} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos 5 \theta \sin 4 \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \text{ Either } \cos 5 \theta=0 \text{$ or $} \sin 4 \theta=0 \text{, also } \theta \in[0,2 \pi] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 5 \theta=(2 n+1) \frac{\pi}{2} \\
& \text{ or } \quad 4 \theta=n \pi \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=(2 n+1) \frac{\pi}{10} \text{ or } \theta=\frac{n \pi}{4} \\
& \therefore \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{10}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{10}, \frac{9 \pi}{10}, \frac{11 \pi}{10}, \frac{13 \pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{17 \pi}{10}, \frac{19 \pi}{10} \\
& \text{ or } \quad 0, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \pi, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{4}, 2 \pi \\
& \therefore \text{ Total number of solutions }=17 \\
& \left(\because \frac{\pi}{2} \text{ and } \frac{3 \pi}{2} \text{ are common }\right)
\end{aligned}$

20177.subject: Chemistry
20177.text: Given that molar conductances for $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$, $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ are 523.28,280.0 and $129.8\Omega^{-1} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively. What is the molar conductivity $\left(\Omega^{-1} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right) of \mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ ?
20177.sol:
According to Kohlrausch law of independent migration of ions, the molar conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution is the sum of the molar conductivities of its constituent ions.

The given molar conductivities are:
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}) = \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{OH}^{-}) = 523.28$
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}) = \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}) = 280.0$
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}) = \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}) + \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}) = 129.8$

We need to find $\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}) + \lambda^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{OH}^{-})$.

Using the given values, we can express $\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH})$ as:
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = \Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}) - \dfrac{1}{2}\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{BaCl}_{2})$

Substituting the values:
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 129.8 + \dfrac{523.28}{2} - \dfrac{280.0}{2}$
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 129.8 + 261.64 - 140.0$
$\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 391.44 - 140.0 = 251.44$

Answer: $251.44$

20206.text: Carbon monoxide is poisonous to human beings because
options: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.
it leads to coagulation of blood.
20206.sol:
Carbon monoxide (CO$) has a very high affinity for haemoglobin, which is approximately 300 times greater than that of oxygen (O_{2}$).

When $CO$ is inhaled, it binds to the iron atom in the haemoglobin molecule to form carboxyhaemoglobin, which is much more stable than oxyhaemoglobin.

This binding prevents haemoglobin from transporting oxygen to the tissues, leading to oxygen deprivation and toxicity.

Answer: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.

20443.subject: Chemistry
20443.text: Para and ortho hydrogen differ in:
20443.sol:
Hydrogen gas exists in two isomeric forms known as ortho-hydrogen and para-hydrogen.

In ortho-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in the same direction (parallel).

In para-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in opposite directions (antiparallel).

Both forms have the same atomic number, the same number of neutrons (zero in the case of protium), and the same size, as they are both molecules of $H_2$.

Therefore, they differ only in the relative orientation of the nuclear spins.

Answer: Spins of protons

20558.subject: Chemistry
20558.text: In the redox reaction between $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-} / \mathrm{H}^{+}$ and sulphite ion, what is the number of moles of electrons involved in producing 3.0 moles of the oxidised product?
20558.sol:
The balanced redox reaction between dichromate ion and sulphite ion in acidic medium is given by:

$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-} + 3\mathrm{SO}_{3}^{2-} + 8\mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-} + 4\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The oxidation half-reaction is the oxidation of sulphite ion to sulphate ion:

$\mathrm{SO}_{3}^{2-} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-} + 2\mathrm{H}^{+} + 2e^{-}$

In this half-reaction, 2 moles of electrons are involved in the production of 1 mole of the oxidised product, which is $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$.

For the production of 3.0 moles of the oxidised product ($\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$), the number of moles of electrons involved is:

$3.0 \text{ moles of } \mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-} \times \dfrac{2 \text{ moles of } e^{-}}{1 \text{ mole of } \mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}} = 6.0 \text{ moles of } e^{-}$

Answer: 6

20708.subject: Chemistry
20708.text: What mass of Silver chloride, in grams, gets precipitated when $150 \mathrm{ ml}$ of $32 \%$ solution of Silver nitrate is reacted with $150 \mathrm{ml}$ of $11 \%$ Sodium chloride solution? Atomic mass in $\mathrm{g} / \mathrm{mol}: \mathrm{Ag}=108, \mathrm{Na}=23, \mathrm{Cl}=35.5, \mathrm{ N}=14, \mathrm{O}=16$
20708.sol:
The chemical reaction is: $AgNO_{3} + NaCl \rightarrow AgCl + NaNO_{3}$.

Molar mass of $AgNO_{3} = 108 + 14 + 3 \times 16 = 170 \text{ g/mol}$.
Molar mass of $NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 \text{ g/mol}$.
Molar mass of $AgCl = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 \text{ g/mol}$.

Assuming the density of the solutions is approximately $1 \text{ g/ml}$, the mass of $150 \text{ ml}$ solution is $150 \text{ g}$.
Mass of $AgNO_{3} = 32\% \text{ of } 150 \text{ g} = 0.32 \times 150 = 48 \text{ g}$.
Moles of $AgNO_{3} = \dfrac{48}{170} \approx 0.2824 \text{ mol}$.

Mass of $NaCl = 11\% \text{ of } 150 \text{ g} = 0.11 \times 150 = 16.5 \text{ g}$.
Moles of $NaCl = \dfrac{16.5}{58.5} \approx 0.2821 \text{ mol}$.

Since the stoichiometry is $1:1$, $NaCl$ is the limiting reagent (as $0.2821 < 0.2824$).
Moles of $AgCl$ formed = Moles of $NaCl = 0.2821 \text{ mol}$.

Mass of $AgCl = 0.2821 \times 143.5 \approx 40.48 \text{ g}$.
Comparing with the given options, the closest value is $40.47 \text{ g}$.

Answer: 40.47

21873.subject: Mathematics
21873.text: Cards are numbered from 12 to 51. Two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement. Find the probability that one card is a multiple of 6 and the other card is a multiple of 8.
21873.sol:
Total number of cards is $51 - 12 + 1 = 40$.

Let $A$ be the set of cards which are multiples of $6$ and $B$ be the set of cards which are multiples of $8$.

$A = \{12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48\} \Rightarrow n(A) = 7$

$B = \{16, 24, 32, 40, 48\} \Rightarrow n(B) = 5$

$A \cap B = \{24, 48\} \Rightarrow n(A \cap B) = 2$

Since two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement, the total number of ordered draws is $40 \times 39 = 1560$.

Let $E_1$ be the event that the first card is in $A$ and the second is in $B$. The number of such draws is $n(A) \times n(B)$ minus the cases where the same card is drawn twice.
$n(E_1) = 7 \times 5 - 2 = 33$

Let $E_2$ be the event that the first card is in $B$ and the second is in $A$. Similarly, the number of such draws is:
$n(E_2) = 5 \times 7 - 2 = 33$

The intersection $E_1 \cap E_2$ represents the event where both cards belong to $A \cap B$. The number of ways to draw two distinct cards from $A \cap B$ is:
$n(E_1 \cap E_2) = 2 \times 1 = 2$

The total number of favorable ordered draws is given by $n(E_1 \cup E_2)$:
$n(E_1 \cup E_2) = n(E_1) + n(E_2) - n(E_1 \cap E_2) = 33 + 33 - 2 = 64$

The required probability is $\dfrac{64}{1560} = \dfrac{8}{195}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{195}$

22196.subject: Mathematics
22196.text: If the direction ratios of two lines are given by $3 l m-4 l n+m n=0$ and $l+2 m+3 n=0$, then the angle between the lines is
22196.sol:
Given the equations for direction ratios $(l, m, n)$ are $3lm - 4ln + mn = 0$ and $l + 2m + 3n = 0$.

From the second equation, $l = -2m - 3n$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$3(-2m - 3n)m - 4(-2m - 3n)n + mn = 0$

$-6m^2 - 9mn + 8mn + 12n^2 + mn = 0$

$-6m^2 + 12n^2 = 0$

$m^2 = 2n^2$, which implies $m = \pm \sqrt{2}n$.

Case 1: $m = \sqrt{2}n$. Then $l = -2(\sqrt{2}n) - 3n = -(2\sqrt{2} + 3)n$.
The direction ratios are $(-(2\sqrt{2} + 3), \sqrt{2}, 1)$. Let this be vector $\vec{v_1}$.

Case 2: $m = -\sqrt{2}n$. Then $l = -2(-\sqrt{2}n) - 3n = (2\sqrt{2} - 3)n$.
The direction ratios are $((2\sqrt{2} - 3), -\sqrt{2}, 1)$. Let this be vector $\vec{v_2}$.

The cosine of the angle $\theta$ between the lines is given by $\cos \theta = \dfrac{|\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2}|}{|\vec{v_1}| |\vec{v_2}|}$.

$\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2} = -(2\sqrt{2} + 3)(2\sqrt{2} - 3) + (\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2}) + (1)(1) = -(8 - 9) - 2 + 1 = 1 - 2 + 1 = 0$.

Since the dot product is $0$, the lines are perpendicular, so $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

22532.subject: Physics
22532.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
22532.text: From a circular disc of radius $R$, a square is cut out with a radius as its diagonal. The centre of mass of remaining portion is at a distance (from the centre)
22532.sol:
Let the radius of the circular disc be $R$. The area of the disc is $A_1 = \pi R^2$. The centre of mass of the disc is at the origin $(0, 0)$.

A square is cut out such that its diagonal is equal to the radius $R$. Let the side of the square be $a$. Then, $a\sqrt{2} = R$, which implies $a = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$. The area of the square is $A_2 = a^2 = \dfrac{R^2}{2}$.

The centre of mass of the square is at the centre of the disc $(0, 0)$. However, the problem implies the square is cut from the disc such that its diagonal lies along a radius. Let the centre of the square be at a distance $d$ from the centre of the disc. Since the diagonal is $R$, the distance from the centre of the square to its vertex is $\dfrac{R}{2}$. If the vertex is at the edge of the disc, the centre of the square is at $d = R - \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

The centre of mass of the remaining portion is given by $X_{cm} = \dfrac{A_1 x_1 - A_2 x_2}{A_1 - A_2}$. Here $x_1 = 0$ and $x_2 = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

$X_{cm} = \dfrac{(\pi R^2)(0) - (R^2/2)(R/2)}{\pi R^2 - R^2/2} = \dfrac{-R^3/4}{R^2(\pi - 1/2)} = \dfrac{-R/4}{(\pi - 1/2)} = \dfrac{-R}{4\pi - 2}$.

The magnitude of the distance is $\dfrac{R}{4\pi - 2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{(4 \pi-2)}$

22894.text: Two spheres of masses $M_1$ and $M_2$ are in air separated by a distance of d m. The gravitational force of attraction between them is F. If the space around the masses is filled with a liquid of density $\rho$, the force between the masses will be
22894.sol:
The gravitational force of attraction between two masses $M_1$ and $M_2$ separated by a distance $d$ is given by Newton's law of gravitation as $F = \dfrac{G M_1 M_2}{d^2}$.

The universal gravitational constant $G$ is independent of the nature of the intervening medium.

Therefore, when the space around the masses is filled with a liquid of density $\rho$, the gravitational force between them remains unchanged and is equal to $F$.

Answer: $F$

23459.text: In the given circuit, if the barrier potential across the diode is 0.5 V , the current in the circuit is:
23459.sol:
The circuit consists of a diode $D$, a resistor $R = 75 \Omega$, and a voltage source $V = 5 \text{ V}$ connected in series.

The diode is forward-biased as the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side of the diode.

The barrier potential $V_{b}$ across the diode is given as $0.5 \text{ V}$.

Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) in the loop:
$V - V_{b} - I \times R = 0$

Substituting the given values:
$5 \text{ V} - 0.5 \text{ V} = I \times 75 \Omega$
$4.5 \text{ V} = I \times 75 \Omega$

Solving for the current $I$:
$I = \dfrac{4.5}{75} \text{ A}$
$I = \dfrac{45}{750} \text{ A}$
$I = \dfrac{3}{50} \text{ A}$
$I = 0.06 \text{ A}$

Converting to milliamperes (mA):
$I = 0.06 \times 1000 \text{ mA} = 60 \text{ mA}$

Answer: 60mA

23490.text: For CE transistor amplifier, the audio signal voltage across the collector resistance of $4 \mathrm{l} \Omega$ is $5 \mathrm{ V}$. If the current amplification factor of the transistor is 100 and base resistance is $2 \mathrm{k} \Omega$, then input signal voltage is
23490.sol:
Given the collector resistance $R_C = 4 \text{ k}\Omega = 4000 \Omega$, the output voltage $V_o = 5 \text{ V}$, and the current amplification factor $\beta = 100$.

The collector current $I_C$ is given by $I_C = \dfrac{V_o}{R_C} = \dfrac{5}{4000} \text{ A} = 1.25 \times 10^{-3} \text{ A} = 1.25 \text{ mA}$.

The base current $I_B$ is related to the collector current by $I_C = \beta I_B$. Thus, $I_B = \dfrac{I_C}{\beta} = \dfrac{1.25 \text{ mA}}{100} = 0.0125 \text{ mA} = 1.25 \times 10^{-5} \text{ A}$.

The input signal voltage $V_i$ is given by $V_i = I_B \times R_B$, where $R_B = 2 \text{ k}\Omega = 2000 \Omega$.

$V_i = (1.25 \times 10^{-5} \text{ A}) \times (2000 \Omega) = 2.5 \times 10^{-2} \text{ V} = 25 \text{ mV}$.

Answer: $25 \mathrm{mV}$

25466.subject: Mathematics
25466.text:
Let $y : (-\infty, \infty) \rightarrow (0, \infty)$ be the solution of the differential equation
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{e^{5x} y^3 + y^3}{e^x + e^x y^4}$,
satisfying $y(0) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. Then the value of $y(\log_e 2)$ is
25466.sol:
The given differential equation is

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{e^{5x} y^3 + y^3}{e^x + e^x y^4}$

Factoring the numerator and denominator, we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^3 (e^{5x} + 1)}{e^x (1 + y^4)}$

Separating the variables $x and y$, we obtain

$\dfrac{1 + y^4}{y^3} dy = \dfrac{e^{5x} + 1}{e^x} dx$

$\left( \dfrac{1}{y^3} + y \right) dy = (e^{4x} + e^{-x}) dx$

Integrating both sides yields

$\int \left( y^{-3} + y \right) dy = \int (e^{4x} + e^{-x}) dx$

$-\dfrac{1}{2y^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{2} = \dfrac{e^{4x}}{4} - e^{-x} + C$

Multiplying by $2$, we get

$y^2 - \dfrac{1}{y^2} = \dfrac{e^{4x}}{2} - 2e^{-x} + 2C$

Using the initial condition $y(0) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, we substitute x = 0 and $y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$:

$\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 - \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2} = \dfrac{e^0}{2} - 2e^0 + 2C$

$\dfrac{1}{2} - 2 = \dfrac{1}{2} - 2 + 2C$

This gives $2C = 0$, so $C = 0$. The equation becomes

$y^2 - \dfrac{1}{y^2} = \dfrac{e^{4x}}{2} - 2e^{-x}$

To find $y(\log_e 2)$, we substitute $x = \log_e 2$ into the equation. We have $e^{4x} = e^{4 \log_e 2} = 16 and e^{-x} = e^{-\log_e 2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$y^2 - \dfrac{1}{y^2} = \dfrac{16}{2} - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$y^2 - \dfrac{1}{y^2} = 8 - 1 = 7$

Let $y^2 = t$. Since $y \in (0, \infty)$, $t > 0$.

$t - \dfrac{1}{t} = 7$

$t^2 - 7t - 1 = 0$

Solving for $t$ using the quadratic formula gives

$t = \dfrac{7 \pm \sqrt{49 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2} = \dfrac{7 \pm \sqrt{53}}{2}$

Since $t = y^2 > 0$, we must choose the positive root:

$y^2 = \dfrac{7 + \sqrt{53}}{2}$

Taking the positive square root since $y > 0$, we get

$y = \sqrt{\dfrac{7 + \sqrt{53}}{2}}$

Given,

We have to choose two distinct points randomly,

Now number of ways of selecting $2$ adjacent dots in row will be$= 6$ {as if you pick any dot then you have pick second dot from remaining $6$ dots, so total ways will be $1 \times C1 6 = 6$}

Similarly, number of ways of selecting $2$ adjacent dots in column$= 6$

$∴$Number of ways of selecting $2$ adjacent dots from the given diagram we will $= 6 \times 7 + 6 \times 7 = 84$

27622.text:
The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is :
A.
B. $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]^{+}, \mathrm{OH}^{-}}[\mathrm{B}]$
C. $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \xrightarrow[\text{ (ii) } \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7} / \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text{(i) }}[\mathrm{C}]$
D. $\mathrm{PhCH}_{2} \mathrm{MgBr}+\mathrm{CO}_{2} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{+}]{\text{Dry ether }}[\mathrm{D}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
27622.sol:
Product [A]: From PhNH₂, steps (1) NaNO₂ + HCl forms diazonium salt, (2) CuCN gives benzonitrile, (3) H₃O⁺/Δ hydrolyzes to benzoic acid (PhCOOH), pKa ≈ 4.2.
Product [B]: From CH₃CH₂CHO, Tollens' oxidation with $[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$ produces acetic acid (CH₃COOH), pKa ≈ 4.8.
Product [C]: From CH₄ + O₂ with heat and Na₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ produces formic acid (HCOOH), pKa ≈ 3.8 (strongest acid).
Product [D]: From PhCH₂MgBr + CO₂, the Grignard reaction produces phenylacetic acid (PhCH₂COOH), pKa ≈ 4.3.
Acidic strength order (lower pKa = stronger): C (3.8) > A (4.2) > D (4.3) > B (4.8).

Partial pressure$=$Total pressure$\times$Mole fraction

Mole fraction$= \dfrac{Numberofmolesofonecomponent}{Totalnumberofmoles}$

29551.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason.

Assertion: Polluted water may have a value of $BOD$ of the order of $17ppm$.

Reason: $BOD$ is a measure of oxygen required to oxidise both the biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic material in water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
29551.sol: The amount of oxygen required by bacteria to break down the organic matter present in a certain volume of a sample of water, is called Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD). The amount of BOD in the water is a measure of the amount of organic material in the water, in terms of how much oxygen will be required to break it down biologically. Clean water would have BOD value of less than $5ppm$ whereas highly polluted water could have a BOD value of $17ppm$ or more.

Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
31304.sol:
Statement I is false because sodium dichromate is deliquescent (absorbs moisture from the atmosphere) and cannot be weighed accurately, so it is not used as a primary standard. Potassium dichromate, however, is a primary standard.

Statement II is false because phenolphthalein is a weak organic acid, not a weak base. It remains largely undissociated in an acidic medium (colorless) and dissociates in a basic medium to give a pink color.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

31454.text: An element $A$ of group $1$ shows similarity to an element $B$ belonging to group $2$. If $A$ has maximum hydration enthalpy in group $1$ then $B$ is
31454.sol:
Hydration enthalpy is inversely related to the size of the ion.

${Li}^{+}$ has maximum hydration enthalpy in group $1$ due to its small size.

Lithium shows diagonal relationship to magnesium.

The similarity between lithium and magnesium is particularly striking and arises because of their similar sizes : atomic radii, Li = 152 pm, Mg = 160 pm; ionic radii : Li+ = 76 pm, Mg2+= 72 pm.

The main points of similarity are

(I)Both lithium and magnesium are harder and lighter (ii) Lithium and magnesium react slowly with water. Their oxides and hydroxides are much less soluble and their hydroxides decompose on heating. Both form a nitride, Li3N and Mg3N2 , by direct combination with nitrogen. (iii) The oxides, Li2O and MgO do not combine with excess oxygen to give any superoxide. (iv) The carbonates of lithium and magnesium decompose easily on heating to form the oxides and CO2 .

Solid hydrogencarbonates are not formed by lithium and magnesium. (v) Both LiCl and MgCl2 are soluble in ethanol. (vi) Both LiCl and MgCl2 are deliquescent and crystallise from aqueous solution as hydrates, LiCl·2H2O and MgCl2 ·6H2O.

So '$B$' is $Mg$.

34966.text: Let a focus of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ be $S(4, 0)$ and its eccentricity be $\dfrac{4}{5}$. If the point $P(3, \alpha)$ lies on $E$ and $O$ is the origin, then the area of $\triangle POS$ is equal to:
34966.sol:
Given the focus of the ellipse $S(4, 0)$, we have $ae = 4$.

Since the eccentricity $e = \dfrac{4}{5}$, we get $a \left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) = 4 \Rightarrow a = 5$.

Using the relation $b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$, we find:

$b^2 = 25 \left(1 - \dfrac{16}{25}\right) = 9$

The equation of the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{25} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$.

Since the point $P(3, \alpha)$ lies on the ellipse, substituting $x = 3$ gives:

$\dfrac{9}{25} + \dfrac{\alpha^2}{9} = 1$

$\dfrac{\alpha^2}{9} = 1 - \dfrac{9}{25} = \dfrac{16}{25}$

$\alpha^2 = \dfrac{144}{25} \Rightarrow |\alpha| = \dfrac{12}{5}$

The coordinates of the vertices of $\triangle POS$ are $O(0, 0)$, $S(4, 0)$, and $P\left(3, \pm \dfrac{12}{5}\right)$.

The area of $\triangle POS$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

Taking $OS$ as the base, the length is $4$, and the height is the absolute value of the y-coordinate of $P$, which is $\dfrac{12}{5}$.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \dfrac{12}{5} = \dfrac{24}{5}$

Answer: $24/5$

39512.subject: Physics
39512.text: Refer to the figure given below. The values of $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ are __________.
39512.sol:
Using the principle of superposition, we analyse the circuit with one source active at a time.

Case 1: Only the $10\text{ V}$ source is active (the $5\text{ V}$ source is replaced by a short circuit).

With the $5\text{ V}$ source shorted, the top and bottom nodes of the bridge are directly connected by a wire, forming a Wheatstone bridge.

Checking for balance:
Left arm ratio: $\dfrac{4}{4} = 1$
Right arm ratio: $\dfrac{2}{2} = 1$

The ratios are equal, so the bridge is balanced. Hence, no current flows through the middle branch connecting the two nodes, and the contribution to $I_2$ from the $10\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance of the balanced bridge:
$(4 + 2)\,\Omega \parallel (4 + 2)\,\Omega = 6\,\Omega \parallel 6\,\Omega = 3\,\Omega$

Total resistance including the series $1\,\Omega$ resistor:
$R_{eq} = 3 + 1 = 4\,\Omega$

Current drawn from the $10\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{1(10V)} = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5\text{ A}$

This current splits equally between the two $6\,\Omega$ branches, so the current through the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor is:
$I_{3(10V)} = \dfrac{2.5}{2} = 1.25\text{ A}$

Case 2: Only the $5\text{ V}$ source is active (the $10\text{ V}$ source is replaced by a short circuit).

Now the $5\text{ V}$ source is applied across the top and bottom nodes, and the $1\,\Omega$ resistor lies in the middle branch between the left and centre nodes.

For the left branch ($4\,\Omega$ and $4\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.
For the right branch ($2\,\Omega$ and $2\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is also $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.

Since both midpoints are at the same potential, no current flows through the $1\,\Omega$ middle branch. Hence, the contribution to $I_1$ from the $5\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance seen by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$(4 + 4)\,\Omega \parallel (2 + 2)\,\Omega = 8\,\Omega \parallel 4\,\Omega = \dfrac{8 \times 4}{8 + 4} = \dfrac{8}{3}\,\Omega$

Total current supplied by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{2(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8/3} = \dfrac{15}{8} = 1.875\text{ A}$

Current through the left branch (which includes the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor):
$I_{3(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8} = 0.625\text{ A}$

Applying superposition:
$I_1 = I_{1(10V)} + I_{1(5V)} = 2.5 + 0 = 2.5\text{ A}$
$I_2 = I_{2(10V)} + I_{2(5V)} = 0 + 1.875 = 1.875\text{ A}$
$I_3 = I_{3(10V)} + I_{3(5V)} = 1.25 + 0.625 = 1.875\text{ A}$

Hence, the correct option is $(1)\ I_1 = 2.5\text{ A},\ I_2 = 1.875\text{ A},\ I_3 = 1.875\text{ A}$.

The relation between the distance travelled $\left(S\right)$ by the train with its initial velocity $\left(u\right)$ and its final velocity $\left(v\right)$ is given by

where, $a$ indicates the retardation of the train.

Substitute the values corresponding to the initial condition into equation (1) and solve to calculate the retardation of the train.

$\begin{cases}0 & = & ( 20{)}^{2} - 2 \times a \times 500 \\ a & = & 0 . 4m / {s}^{2}\end{cases}$

43151.subject: Physics
43151.text: An object of uniform density rolls up the curved path with the initial velocity $v_0$ as shown in the figure. If the maximum height attained by an object is $\dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}$ ($g$ = acceleration due to gravity), the object is a _______.
43151.sol:
By the law of conservation of mechanical energy, the total initial kinetic energy of the rolling object is converted into potential energy at the maximum height.

Total initial kinetic energy for an object rolling without slipping is given by:
$K = K_{\text{translational}} + K_{\text{rotational}}$
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

Substituting $\omega = \dfrac{v_0}{R}$ and $I = mk^2$ (where $k$ is the radius of gyration):
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}(mk^2)\left(\dfrac{v_0}{R}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2\left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$

The potential energy at the maximum height $h$ is:
$U = mgh$

Given $h = \dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}$, we have:
$U = mg\left(\dfrac{7v_0^2}{10g}\right) = \dfrac{7}{10}mv_0^2$

Equating kinetic and potential energy ($K = U$):
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2\left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = \dfrac{7}{10}mv_0^2$

$1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{14}{10} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$\dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{7}{5} - 1 = \dfrac{2}{5}$

The moment of inertia is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2$, which corresponds to a solid sphere.

Answer: solid sphere

43876.subject: Physics
43876.text: Consider two containers $A and B$ containing monoatomic gases at the same Pressure $\left(P\right)$, Volume $\left(V\right)$ and Temperature $\left(T\right)$. The gas in $A$ is compressed isothermally to $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of its original volume while the gas in $B$ is compressed adiabatically to $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of its original volume. The ratio of final pressure of gas in $B$ to that of gas in $A$ is
43876.sol:
In an isothermal process the temperature is constant.

$PV = nRT$

So, it can be written that

$PV = {P}_{A}\left(\dfrac{V}{8}\right) ⇒ {P}_{A} = 8P$

In an adiabatic process,

$P{V}^{\gamma} =$constant

$\gamma$ for monoatomic gas is $\dfrac{5}{3}$

So, it can be written

$\dfrac{{P}_{B}}{P} = \left(\dfrac{V}{\dfrac{V}{8}}\right)\dfrac{5}{3} ⇒ {P}_{B} = 32P$

Thus, the ratio of the pressures is

$\dfrac{{P}_{B}}{{P}_{A}} = \dfrac{32P}{8P} = 4$

46493.text: The half life of a radioactive substance is 3.6 days. How much of 20 mg of this radioactive substance will remain after 36 days?
46493.sol:
Half life $T_{1 / 2}=3.6$ days
Initial quantity $N_0=20 \mathrm{mg}$
Total time $=36$ days
The number of half lives
$n=\frac{t}{T_{1 / 2}}=\frac{36}{3.6}=10$
Hence, mass of radioactive substance left after 10 half lives
$N=N_0 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n=20 \times \frac{1}{1024}=0.019 \mathrm{mg}$

As the block $A$ moves with velocity $0.15 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$, it compresses thespring which pushes $B$ towards right. $A$ goes on compressing the spring till the velocity acquired by $B$ becomes equal to the velocity of $A$, ie, $0.15 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$. 57585.subject: Chemistry
57585.text: Identify the major product of dehydrohalogenation of $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_3$.
57585.sol:
Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_3$) involves the removal of a hydrogen atom from a $\beta$-carbon and the bromine atom from the $\alpha$-carbon.

There are two $\beta$-carbons in 2-bromobutane, leading to two possible alkene products:
1. Removal of hydrogen from C1 yields 1-butene ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH}_2$).
2. Removal of hydrogen from C3 yields 2-butene ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_3$).

According to Zaitsev's rule, the major product in a dehydrohalogenation reaction is the more substituted alkene, as it is thermodynamically more stable.

2-butene is a disubstituted alkene, whereas 1-butene is a monosubstituted alkene.

Thus, 2-butene ($\text{H}_3\text{C-CH=CH-CH}_3$) is the major product.

Answer: $\text{H}_3\text{C-CH=CH-CH}_3$

58605.text: What is the oxidation number of Cl in $\text{HOClO}_2$?
58605.sol:
Let the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in $\text{HOClO}_2$ (which is $\text{HClO}_3$) be $x$.

The oxidation number of hydrogen ($\text{H}$) is $+1$ and that of oxygen ($\text{O}$) is $-2$.

The sum of the oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

$+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0$

$x - 5 = 0$

$x = +5$

The oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in $\text{HOClO}_2$ is $+5$.

Answer: $+5$

$d = \dfrac{2 \times 225}{75}$

$d = \dfrac{450}{75} = 6.0\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$

63170.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, $C = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$ and $AB = C$, then the inverse of matrix B is
63170.sol:
Given $AB = C$

Taking inverse on both sides, we get $(AB)^{-1} = C^{-1}$

$B^{-1}A^{-1} = C^{-1}$

Multiplying both sides by $A$ on the right, we get $B^{-1} = C^{-1}A$

We have $C = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$

$|C| = 7(6) - 3(0) = 42$

$C^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{42}\begin{bmatrix} 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$

Now, $B^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{42}\begin{bmatrix} 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

$B^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{42}\begin{bmatrix} 18+3 & 6-6 \\ 0-7 & 0+14 \end{bmatrix}$

$B^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{42}\begin{bmatrix} 21 & 0 \\ -7 & 14 \end{bmatrix}$

$B^{-1} = \dfrac{7}{42}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

64464.text: The line passing through the point $(5,1, a) and (3, b, 1)$ crosses the yz-plane at $\left(0, \frac{17}{2}, \frac{-13}{2}\right)$, then the value of $2 a+3 \mathrm{~b}$ is
64464.sol:
The line through $P_1 = (5, 1, a)$ and $P_2 = (3, b, 1)$ has direction ratios determined by their coordinates. The symmetric form of its equation is:

$\frac{x - 5}{3 - 5} = \frac{y - 1}{b - 1} = \frac{z - a}{1 - a} = \lambda$

which simplifies to:

$\frac{x - 5}{-2} = \frac{y - 1}{b - 1} = \frac{z - a}{1 - a} = \lambda$

This line intersects the yz-plane where $x = 0$. Substituting gives:

$\frac{0 - 5}{-2} = \lambda$

so $\lambda = \frac{5}{2}$.

Using the known intersection point $\left(0, \frac{17}{2}, \frac{-13}{2}\right) and \lambda = \frac{5}{2}$, solve for $b$ from the y-component:

$\frac{\frac{17}{2} - 1}{b - 1} = \frac{5}{2}$

$\frac{\frac{15}{2}}{b - 1} = \frac{5}{2}$

$\frac{15}{b - 1} = 5$

$b - 1 = 3$

$b = 4$

Similarly, from the z-component:

$\frac{\frac{-13}{2} - a}{1 - a} = \frac{5}{2}$

$\frac{-13 - 2a}{2(1 - a)} = \frac{5}{2}$

$-13 - 2a = 5(1 - a)$

$-13 - 2a = 5 - 5a$

$3a = 18$

$a = 6$

Thus, $2a + 3b = 2 \times 6 + 3 \times 4 = 12 + 12 = 24$.

$\boxed{24}$

65854.subject: Physics
65854.text:
The magnetic moment of electron due to orbital motion is proportional to
(n$ = principal quantum number)$
65854.sol:
Magnetic moment of an electron due to orbital motion is given by $\mu = I A$.

Current $I = \dfrac{e}{T} = \dfrac{e v}{2 \pi r}$ and Area $A = \pi r^2$.

$\mu = \left(\dfrac{e v}{2 \pi r}\right) (\pi r^2) = \dfrac{e v r}{2}$

Multiplying and dividing by mass $m$, we get $\mu = \dfrac{e}{2m} (m v r) = \dfrac{e}{2m} L$

From Bohr's quantization rule, angular momentum $L = \dfrac{n h}{2 \pi}$.

$\mu = \dfrac{e}{2m} \left(\dfrac{n h}{2 \pi}\right) =n \left(\dfrac{e h}{4 \pi m}\right)

Therefore, \mu \propto n$.

Answer: $n$

66041.text: Capacitors of capacities $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in series. If the combination is connected to a supply of V volt then the potential difference across capacitor $C_2$ is
66041.sol:
In series combination, the equivalent capacitance is $C_{eq} = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$.

The charge on each capacitor is the same and is given by $Q = C_{eq} V = \left( \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} \right) V$.

The potential difference across capacitor $C_2$ is $V_2 = \dfrac{Q}{C_2}$.

Substituting the value of $Q$, we get $V_2 = \dfrac{C_1 V}{C_1 + C_2}$.

68173.subject: Physics
68173.text: A liquid drop having surface energy E is sprayed into 512 droplets of same size. The final surface energy is
68173.sol:
The surface energy of a sphere is directly proportional to its surface area. Initially, with a drop of radius $R$ and surface tension $T$, the energy is $E = 4\pi R^2 T$.

After spraying into $N = 512$ droplets, volume conservation requires $R^3 = N r^3$, where $r$ is the radius of each small droplet. Solving yields $r = R / 8$.

The final surface energy is the sum over all droplets: $E' = N \cdot 4\pi r^2 T$. Substituting $r = R / 8$ gives $E' = N \cdot 4\pi (R^2 / 64) T = (N / 64) \cdot 4\pi R^2 T$.

Since $E = 4\pi R^2 T$, it follows that $E' = (512 / 64) E = 8E$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

68504.text: A particle at rest starts moving with constant angular acceleration '$\alpha$' in a circular path of radius 'r'. At certain instant, the magnitude of centripetal acceleration is $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ the tangential acceleration. The relation between linear speed (V) and angular acceleration ($\alpha$) is
68504.sol:
The tangential acceleration of the particle is given by $a_t = r\alpha$.

The centripetal acceleration of the particle is given by $a_c = \dfrac{V^2}{r}$.

According to the given condition, the magnitude of centripetal acceleration is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the tangential acceleration:

$a_c = \dfrac{1}{3} a_t$

Substituting the expressions for $a_c$ and $a_t$:

$\dfrac{V^2}{r} = \dfrac{1}{3} (r\alpha)$

$V^2 = \dfrac{r^2 \alpha}{3}$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$V = r\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{3}}$

Answer: $V = r\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{3}}$

68608.subject: Physics
68608.text: A radioactive element has rate of disintegration 9000 disintegration per minute at a particular instant. After two minutes it becomes 3000 disintegration per minute. The decay constant per minute is
68608.sol:
The radioactive decay formula $R = R_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ relates the disintegration rate $R$ at time $t$ to the initial rate $R_0$ and decay constant $\lambda$.

Given $R_0 = 9000$ disintegrations/min, $R = 3000$ disintegrations/min at $t = 2$ min:

$3000 = 9000 e^{-2\lambda}$

Simplifying gives $\frac{1}{3} = e^{-2\lambda}$

Taking natural logarithms of both sides:

$\ln\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -2\lambda$

Using the logarithmic identity $\ln\left(\frac{1}{a}\right) = -\ln(a)$:

$-\ln(3) = -2\lambda$

Solving for $\lambda$ yields:

$\lambda = \frac{\ln(3)}{2}$

This matches option A.

69731.text: A celsius and a Fahrenheit thermometer are dipped in boiling water. The temperature of water is lowered until the Farenheit thermometer shows $140^{}^{\circ}$. What is the fall in temperature on the Celsius thermometer?
69731.sol:
The initial temperature of boiling water is $100^{}^{\circ}$ C, which corresponds to $212^{}^{\circ}$ F.

The final temperature is given as $140^{}^{\circ}$ F.

The relationship between the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales is given by:

$\dfrac{C}{5} = \dfrac{F - 32}{9}$

Substituting $F = 140$:

$\dfrac{C}{5} = \dfrac{140 - 32}{9} = \dfrac{108}{9} = 12$

$C = 60^{}^{\circ}$ C

The fall in temperature on the Celsius thermometer is the difference between the initial and final temperatures:

$\Delta C = 100^{}^{\circ} \text{ C} - 60^{}^{\circ} \text{ C} = 40^{}^{\circ} \text{ C}$

Answer: $40^{}^{\circ}$ C

69919.subject: Physics
69919.text: A carnot engine having efficiency $\dfrac{1}{6}$, operates between the source temperature $T_H$ and the sink temperature $T_C$. Its efficiency increases to $\dfrac{1}{3}$, when $T_C$ is decreased by 64 K. The temperatures $T_H$ and $T_C$ are repectively
69919.sol:
The efficiency of a Carnot engine is given by $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$.

Initially, $\eta = \dfrac{1}{6}$, so:

$\dfrac{1}{6} = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$

$\dfrac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}$

$T_C = \dfrac{5}{6} T_H$

When $T_C$ is decreased by $64 \text{ K}$, the new sink temperature is $T_C - 64$. The new efficiency is $\dfrac{1}{3}$.

$\dfrac{1}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{T_C - 64}{T_H}$

$\dfrac{T_C - 64}{T_H} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\dfrac{T_C}{T_H} - \dfrac{64}{T_H} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Substitute $\dfrac{T_C}{T_H} = \dfrac{5}{6}$ into the equation:

$\dfrac{5}{6} - \dfrac{64}{T_H} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\dfrac{64}{T_H} = \dfrac{5}{6} - \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\dfrac{64}{T_H} = \dfrac{5 - 4}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$T_H = 64 \times 6 = 384 \text{ K}$

Now, find $T_C$:

$T_C = \dfrac{5}{6} T_H = \dfrac{5}{6} \times 384 = 5 \times 64 = 320 \text{ K}$

Therefore, $T_H = 384 \text{ K}$ and $T_C = 320 \text{ K}$.

71293.text: The enzyme that facilitates local unwinding of DNA duplex during transcription is-------------------.
71293.sol:
During transcription, RNA polymerase binds to the promoter region of the DNA and initiates the process. It not only catalyzes the polymerization of RNA but also facilitates the local unwinding (opening) of the DNA double helix to form the transcription bubble, allowing the template strand to be read.

DNA helicase is responsible for unwinding DNA during replication, not transcription. DNA polymerase synthesizes DNA during replication, and DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

Answer: RNA polymerase

72352.subject: Physics
72352.text: The thin prism having refracting angle $10^{}^{\circ}$ is made of glass of refractive index $1.42$. This prism is combined with another thin prism of glass of refractive index $1.7$. This combination produces dispersion without deviation. The refracting angle of the second prism is
72352.sol:
For a thin prism, the deviation produced is given by $\delta = (\mu - 1)A$.

For the combination to produce dispersion without deviation, the net deviation must be zero. This means the deviations produced by the two prisms must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

$(\mu_1 - 1)A_1 = (\mu_2 - 1)A_2$

Substituting the given values:

$(1.42 - 1) \times 10^{}^{\circ} = (1.7 - 1) \times A_2$

$0.42 \times 10^{}^{\circ} = 0.7 \times A_2$

$4.2^{}^{\circ} = 0.7 A_2$

$A_2 = \dfrac{4.2^{}^{\circ}}{0.7} = 6^{}^{\circ}$

Answer: $6^{}^{\circ}$

76443.subject: Mathematics
76443.text:
Passage: Let $k$ be the area between the curve $y=\sin x$ and x-axis in the interval $\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$.

Question: What is the area between the curve $y=\cos x$ and the x-axis in the interval $\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ ?
76443.sol:
$k = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \sin x \, dx$

Let the required area be $A = \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} \cos x \, dx$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - t$, we get $dx = -dt$

When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $t = 0$

$A = \int_{\pi/4}^{0} \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right) (-dt)$

$A = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \sin t \, dt$

$A = k$

Answer: $k$

76890.subject: Mathematics
76890.text:
Paragraph : Consider the integrals
$\mathrm{I}_1=\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \frac{d x}{1+\sqrt{\tan x}} \text{ and } \mathrm{I}_2=\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x} d x}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}}.$Question :
What is $\mathrm{I}_1$ equal to?
76890.sol:
Consider the integrals
$\mathrm{I}_1=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{d x}{1+\sqrt{\tan x}}$
and $\quad \mathrm{I}_2=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x} d x}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}}$
Let
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{I}_1 & =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{d x}{1+\sqrt{\tan x}} ...(i)\\
& =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x}+\sqrt{\sin x}} d x \\
& =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}}{\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)} d x \\
& {\left[\because\left(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{3}-x\right)=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right] } \\
& =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}} d x...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Adding (i) and (ii) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \mathrm{I}_1 & =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} 1 d x=[x]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{I}_1 & =\frac{\pi}{12}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}_2=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}} d x ...(i)\\
& \mathrm{I}_2=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}}{\sqrt{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}+\sqrt{\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}} d x \\
& \mathrm{I}_2=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x}+\sqrt{\sin x}} d x...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Adding (i) and (ii) we get
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & & 2 \mathrm{I}_2 & =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}} d x \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \mathrm{I}_2 & =\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} 1 d x=[x]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{I}_2 & =\frac{\pi}{12} .
\end{array}
$ I_1=$\frac{\pi}{12}$

81536.text: Which of the following statement, about the advantage of roasting of sulphide ore before reduction is not true?
options: The $\Delta \mathrm{G}_f^{\text{o }}$ of the sulphide is greater than those for $\mathrm{CS}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{ S} .$

84069.sol:

Fundamentaly, the pumping action of heart generates blood flow. The contraction of atria is initiated and activated by sinoatrial node (SA node-Pacemaker), which spreads waves of contraction across the wall of atria via muscle fibres at regular intervals.

85137.subject: Zoology
85137.text: Animals have the innate ability to escape from predation. Examples for the same are given below. Select the incorrect example.
options: enlargement of body size by swallowing air in puffer fish
85137.sol:
Colour change in chameleon and melanism in moths are examples of camouflage in animals adapted to prevent predation from prey. As a defence mechanism puffers have the ability to inflate rapidly, filling their extremely elastic stomach with water (or air) until they are almost spherical. This prevents them from being identified by the predator. But poison fangs in snakes are a method adopted for preying and not escaping predation.
Related Theory
Prey species have defense adaptations that help them escape predation. These defenses may be mechanical, chemical, physical, or behavioural. Camouflage is the ability of an organism to blend in with its surroundings.
It can be as simple as being the predominant colour of surrounding vegetation, or it can define an organism's complete morphology, like this walking stick. It is considered as a great defensive strategy, as evidenced by its widespread use in nature.

91714.text: The equations $kx^{2} + x + k = 0$ and $kx^{2} + kx + 1 = 0$ have exactly one root in common for
91714.sol:
Let $\alpha$ be the common root
$⇒k{\alpha}^{2} + \alpha + k = 0$
$k{\alpha}^{2} + k\alpha + 1 = 0$
On solving, we get,

$\dfrac{\alpha2}{1 - k^{2}} = \dfrac{α}{k^{2} - k} = \dfrac{1}{k^{2} - k}$
$\dfrac{{\alpha}^{2}}{\alpha} = \dfrac{1 - k^{2}}{k^{2} - k}$ and $\dfrac{\alpha}{1} = \dfrac{k^{2} - k}{k^{2} - k}$
$⇒\alpha = \dfrac{1 - k^{2}}{k^{2} - k} = 1 ⇒ k^{2} - k = 1 - k^{2}$
$⇒2k^{2} - k - 1 = 0 ⇒ k = - \dfrac{1}{2}, 1$
For $k = 1,$ equations are identical, thus not possible
Hence, $k = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

⇒ $ \text{ and } t = 4 e ⁡ = 4 \times \dfrac{5}{8} = 2 \text{.} 5 \text\sec$

The distance $\text{AB} = u ⁡ \text\sin 3 {0}^{ο} t + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{g} \text\sin 3 {0}^{ο} t^{2}$

Self-inductance of the solenoid is given by

$L = \mu\left(r\right)n^{2}\pia^{2}l$

So, the self-inductance can be written as

$L = {\mu}_{1}n^{2}l\pib^{2}{\left|{}_{0 < r < b} + {\mu}_{2}n^{2}l\left(\pia^{2} - \pib^{2}\right)\right|}_{b < r < a}$

$= \pin^{2}l \left[{\mu}_{1}b^{2} + {\mu}_{2} \left(a^{2} - b^{2}\right)\right]

$

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}or{v}_{rms} ∝ \sqrt{T}$

${v}_{rms}$ is to reduce two times, i.e. the temperature of the gas will have to reduce four times or

$\dfrac{T'}{T} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

During the adiabatic process,

$T ⁡ V{⁡}^{\gamma - 1} = T{⁡}^{'}V{⁡}^{' \gamma - 1}$

or $\dfrac{V{⁡}^{'}}{V} = \left(\dfrac{T}{T'}\right)\dfrac{1}{\gamma - 1}$

$= {\left(4\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{1.5 - 1}} = {4}^{2} = 16$

$∴V^{'} = 16V$

98916.text: Which of the following species has the same& hybridization as $C$ in ${CH}_{2} = {CH}_{2}$?
98916.sol:
Hybridization is the intermixing of the atomic orbitals that have similar or comparable energies.

Hybridisation can be calculated by the electron pair number method.

$ElectronPairHybridization2sp3{sp}^{2}4{sp}^{3}5{sp}^{3}d6{sp}^{3}d^{2}7{sp}^{3}d^{3}$

Electron pair can be calculated as the given below.

$E. P = \dfrac{valenceelectronofcentralatom + monovalentatom + negativecharge - positvecharge}{2}$

For ${CO}_{3}^{2 -}$

$E. P = \dfrac{4 + 0 + 2 + 0}{2} = 3 = {sp}^{2}$

For ${XeF}_{4}$

$E. P = \dfrac{8 + 4 + 2 + 0}{2} = 6 = {sp}^{3}d^{2}$

For ${PCl}_{3}$

$E. P = \dfrac{5 + 3 + 2 + 0}{2} = 4 = {sp}^{3}$

For ${I}_{3}^{-}$

100684.subject: Physics
100684.text:
Match the physical situations involving a block of mass $m$ on a smooth inclined plane of angle $\theta$ (List-I) with their corresponding expressions (List-II).

List-IList-II
A. Acceleration of a block sliding freely down the inclineI. $mg \cos\theta$
B. Normal reaction on a block sliding freely down the inclineII. $g \sin\theta$
C. Minimum horizontal force required to keep the block stationaryIII. $\dfrac{mg}{\cos\theta}$
D. Normal reaction on a block kept stationary by a horizontal forceIV. $mg \tan\theta$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
100684.sol:
A. For a block sliding freely down a smooth incline, the only force along the incline is $mg \sin\theta$. Acceleration $a = \dfrac{mg \sin\theta}{m} = g \sin\theta$.

B. The force perpendicular to the incline is balanced. Normal reaction $N = mg \cos\theta$.

C. To keep the block stationary with a horizontal force $F$, the component of $F$ up the incline must balance the weight component down the incline: $F \cos\theta = mg \sin\theta \Rightarrow F = mg \tan\theta$.

D. The normal reaction in this case balances both the perpendicular component of weight and the perpendicular component of the horizontal force: $N = mg \cos\theta + F \sin\theta$. Substituting $F = mg \tan\theta$, we get $N = mg \cos\theta + (mg \tan\theta) \sin\theta = mg \left(\cos\theta + \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = \dfrac{mg}{\cos\theta}$.

Therefore, the correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

100700.subject: Physics
100700.text: A block of mass $4 \text{ kg}$ is pulled up along a rough inclined plane of angle $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal by a force of $70 \text{ N}$ acting parallel to the plane. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, what is the acceleration of the block? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$)
100700.sol:
Forces acting on the block along the inclined plane are:
1. Applied force $F = 70 \text{ N}$ (upwards)
2. Component of weight $mg \sin 30^{\circ}$ (downwards)
3. Kinetic friction $f_k = \mu_k N = \mu_k mg \cos 30^{\circ}$ (downwards)

Calculating the downward forces:
$mg \sin 30^{\circ} = 4 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 20 \text{ N}$
$f_k = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 4 \times 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 30 \text{ N}$

Net force acting up the plane:
$F_{\text{net}} = F - (mg \sin 30^{\circ} + f_k)$
$F_{\text{net}} = 70 - (20 + 30) = 20 \text{ N}$

Using Newton's second law:
$a = \dfrac{F_{\text{net}}}{m} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

Answer: $5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

100884.subject: Physics
100884.text: An electric motor consumes an input power of $10\text{ kW}$ and operates with an efficiency of $80\%$. It is used to pull a block of mass $400\text{ kg}$ horizontally across a rough surface at a constant speed. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is $0.5$, what is the speed of the block? (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$)
100884.sol:
The useful mechanical power output of the motor is a fraction of the input electrical power, determined by its efficiency.

$P_{\text{out}} = \eta \times P_{\text{in}}$
$P_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{80}{100} \times 10000\text{ W} = 8000\text{ W}$

The frictional force acting on the block on a horizontal surface is given by $f = \mu_k mg$.
$f = 0.5 \times 400 \times 10 = 2000\text{ N}$

Since the block moves at a constant speed, the pulling force $F$ exerted by the motor must exactly balance the frictional force.
$F = f = 2000\text{ N}$

Using the relation between power, force, and velocity ($P = F \times v$):
$8000 = 2000 \times v$
$v = \dfrac{8000}{2000} = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$

Answer: $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$

101182.subject: Physics
101182.text:
A uniform circular ring and a uniform circular disc, both having the same original mass $M$ and radius $R$, have a sector corresponding to an angle of $90^{\circ}$ removed from them. Match the objects in List-I with their respective moments of inertia about an axis passing through their centre and perpendicular to their plane in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Remaining part of the ring(I) $\dfrac{3}{4} M R^2$
(B) Remaining part of the disc(II) $\dfrac{3}{8} M R^2$
(C) Removed sector of the ring(III) $\dfrac{1}{4} M R^2$
(D) Removed sector of the disc(IV) $\dfrac{1}{8} M R^2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
101182.sol:
When a $90^{\circ}$ sector is removed, the fraction of mass removed is $\dfrac{90^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$. The fraction of mass remaining is $\dfrac{3}{4}$.

For a ring, the moment of inertia of any sector about the central axis is $I = m R^2$, where $m$ is the mass of that specific sector.
(A) Remaining part of the ring: mass $m = \dfrac{3}{4} M$, so $I = \dfrac{3}{4} M R^2$ (Matches I).
(C) Removed sector of the ring: mass $m = \dfrac{1}{4} M$, so $I = \dfrac{1}{4} M R^2$ (Matches III).

For a disc, the moment of inertia of any sector about the central axis is $I = \dfrac{1}{2} m R^2$.
(B) Remaining part of the disc: mass $m = \dfrac{3}{4} M$, so $I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{3}{4} M\right) R^2 = \dfrac{3}{8} M R^2$ (Matches II).
(D) Removed sector of the disc: mass $m = \dfrac{1}{4} M$, so $I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{4} M\right) R^2 = \dfrac{1}{8} M R^2$ (Matches IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

103187.text: The \(V-I\) graph for a conductor at temperature \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) are as shown in the figure. \(T_2-T_1\) is proportional to
103187.sol:
\(V-I\) graph for conductor at temperature \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) is shown in the figure.

We know that resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its temperature.
\($\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Hence, } & R_1 \propto T_1 \Rightarrow \tan \theta \propto T_1 \\
\Rightarrow & \tan \theta=K T_1 \quad \ldots (i) \\
\text{and } & R_2 \propto T_2 \\
\Rightarrow & \tan \left(90^{\circ}-\theta\right) \propto T_2 \\
\Rightarrow & \cot \theta \propto T_2 \\
\Rightarrow & \cot \theta=K T_2 \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{array}$\(\therefore\) From $Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get\begin{aligned}
& K T_2-K T_1=\cot \theta-\tan \theta \\
& K\left(T_2-T_1\right)=\frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}-\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} \\
& \Rightarrow T_2-T_1=\frac{\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta}{K \sin \theta \cos \theta} \\
& \Rightarrow T_2-T_1=\frac{\cos 2 \theta}{\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 \theta} \Rightarrow T_2-T_1=\frac{2 \cot 2 \theta}{K} \\
& \Rightarrow T_2-T_1 \propto \cot 2 \theta \\
\end{aligned}\)$

105434.subject: Physics
105434.text:
Data recorded during an experiment to measure the diameter of a sphere using a Vernier calliper ($1$ main scale division = $1$ mm, $10$ Vernier scale divisions = $9$ main scale divisions) is given below:

Condition 1: Jaws fully closed
Main Scale Reading: $0$
Vernier Scale Alignment: Vernier zero is to the right of main scale zero; $6^{th}$ division coincides.

Condition 2: Measuring sphere diameter
Main Scale Reading: $2.4$ cm
Vernier Scale Alignment: $8^{th}$ division coincides.

The actual diameter of the sphere is:
105434.sol:
The least count (LC) of the Vernier calliper is calculated as:

$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ MSD} - 1 \text{ VSD} = 1 \text{ mm} - 0.9 \text{ mm} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.01 \text{ cm}$

Since the Vernier zero is to the right of the main scale zero, the instrument has a positive zero error.

$\text{Zero error} = +n \times \text{LC} = +6 \times 0.01 \text{ cm} = +0.06 \text{ cm}$

The observed reading for the sphere's diameter is:

$\text{Observed reading} = \text{MSR} + (\text{VSR} \times \text{LC}) = 2.4 \text{ cm} + (8 \times 0.01 \text{ cm}) = 2.48 \text{ cm}$

The actual diameter is obtained by subtracting the zero error from the observed reading:

$\text{Actual diameter} = \text{Observed reading} - \text{Zero error}$

$\text{Actual diameter} = 2.48 \text{ cm} - (+0.06 \text{ cm}) = 2.42 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $2.42$ cm

105493.subject: Physics
105493.text:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below:

A. The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

B. The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

C. The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (light emitting diode) source of light.

D. The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
E. Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/electromagnetic waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
105493.sol:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, 

Maximum kinetic energy, $K{E}_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{max}^{2} = hf - ϕ$, where, ${v}_{max}$ is maximum velocity of photoelectrons, $h$ is Planck's constant, $f$ is frequency of incident light and $ϕ$ is work function of metal.

From above relation, we can see that the square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

If we increase the intensity of the incident radiation by keeping the frequency constant, then the value of saturation current increases in proportion to the intensity of the incident radiation. Thus, saturation current decreases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is directly proportional to the light frequency, and it remains constant as light amplitude or power of source increases.

Photoelectric effect cannot be explained on the basis of wave nature because experimentally a particular energy called the work function of the metal surface in needed to eject electrons from surface, irrespective of the time for which light is incident. 

Photoelectric effect can be explained by particle nature of light (i.e. quantum theory). Threshold wavelength is maximum wavelength at which emission takes place.

108982.subject: Chemistry
108982.text:
For the reaction of steam on red hot iron:
$3\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})$
The value of $K_c$ is $2.5$ at $1000 \mathrm{~K}$. What will be the value of $K_p$ for this reaction at the same temperature?
(Given: $\mathrm{R} = 0.083 \mathrm{~L~bar~K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
108982.sol:
For the given heterogeneous reaction:
$3\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta n_g$) is calculated by considering only the gaseous products and reactants, strictly ignoring the solid species.
$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of } \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) - \text{moles of } \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 4 - 4 = 0$

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = 0$:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^0 = K_c$

Therefore, $K_p = 2.5$.

Including solid species in the calculation would incorrectly give $\Delta n_g = -2$, leading to the wrong answer $3.6 \times 10^{-4}$.

Answer: $2.5$

111181.subject: Chemistry
111181.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In one formula unit of potash alum, the total number of cations equals the total number of anions, but this equality of numbers is not a necessary condition for its electrical neutrality.
Reason (R): For an ionic compound to be electrically neutral, only the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge, which can happen even if the number of cations and anions are different.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
111181.sol:
The chemical formula of potash alum is $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

In one formula unit, there are $4$ cations ($2\text{K}^+$ and $2\text{Al}^{3+}$) and $4$ anions ($4\text{SO}_4^{2-}$). Thus, the number of cations equals the number of anions.

However, electrical neutrality simply means that the total positive charge balances the total negative charge. The total positive charge is $(2 \times +1) + (2 \times +3) = +8$. The total negative charge is $4 \times -2 = -8$.

Charge balance does not require an equal number of particles. For instance, in $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$ alone, there are $2$ cations and $1$ anion, yet it is electrically neutral. Therefore, the equality of the number of cations and anions in potash alum is a stoichiometric coincidence of its specific composition, not a direct consequence of the requirement for electrical neutrality.

Assertion (A) is correct. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact logical explanation for why the equality of ion counts in Assertion (A) is not a strict requirement for neutrality. Hence, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion

114401.subject: Chemistry
114401.text:
The standard reduction potentials of halogens are given below:
$E^{\circ}_{F_2/F^-} = 2.87 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{Cl_2/Cl^-} = 1.36 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{Br_2/Br^-} = 1.09 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{I_2/I^-} = 0.54 \text{ V}$

Consider the following statements:
I. $F_2$ is the strongest oxidizing agent among them.
II. $I_2$ can displace $Br^-$ from its aqueous solution.
III. $Cl_2$ can oxidize $I^-$ to $I_2$.
IV. $Br^-$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Cl^-$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
114401.sol:
Statement I is correct: A higher standard reduction potential indicates a stronger tendency to get reduced, making $F_2$ the strongest oxidizing agent.

Statement II is incorrect: For $I_2$ to displace $Br^-$, the reaction $I_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2I^- + Br_2$ must be spontaneous. The standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{I_2/I^-} - E^{\circ}_{Br_2/Br^-} = 0.54 - 1.09 = -0.55 \text{ V}$. Since $E^{\circ}_{cell}$ is negative, the reaction cannot occur.

Statement III is correct: For $Cl_2$ to oxidize $I^-$, the reaction $Cl_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + I_2$ must be spontaneous. $E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{Cl_2/Cl^-} - E^{\circ}_{I_2/I^-} = 1.36 - 0.54 = +0.82 \text{ V}$. Since $E^{\circ}_{cell}$ is positive, the reaction is spontaneous.

Statement IV is correct: A lower standard reduction potential for a halogen means its corresponding halide ion has a stronger tendency to get oxidized. Since $E^{\circ}_{Br_2/Br^-} < E^{\circ}_{Cl_2/Cl^-}$, $Br^-$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Cl^-$.

Thus, statements I, III, and IV are correct, making a total of 3 correct statements.

Answer: 3

118252.subject: Chemistry
118252.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reaction of alkyl halides with $\text{KCN}$ yields alkyl cyanides as major products, whereas with $\text{AgCN}$ it yields isocyanides.
Reason (R): $\text{KCN}$ is mainly covalent in nature, whereas $\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
118252.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. Alkyl halides react with $\text{KCN}$ to form alkyl cyanides as the major product, while the reaction with $\text{AgCN}$ yields alkyl isocyanides as the major product.

Reason (R) is incorrect. The actual reason is that $\text{KCN}$ is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions ($\text{CN}^{-}$) in solution. Since both carbon and nitrogen can donate electron pairs, the attack occurs mainly through carbon because $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds are stronger than $\text{C}-\text{N}$ bonds. In contrast, $\text{AgCN}$ is mainly covalent in nature, so only the nitrogen atom is free to donate an electron pair, resulting in the formation of isocyanides.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

120860.subject: Chemistry
120860.text:
Which of the following statements are true about carbohydrates?
(i) Monosaccharides can be hydrolysed.
(ii) The two monosaccharide units obtained on hydrolysis of a disaccharide can either be same or different.
(iii) Polysaccharides are now sweet in taste.
(iv) All monosaccharides are not reducing. sugars.
120860.sol:
(i) Monosaccharides are smallest carbohydrates that cannot be hydrolysed.
So, statement (i) is not true.
(ii) Disaccharides are made up of two units of monosaccharides, so their hydrolysis will also give two monosaccharide unit that can be same or different.
e.g., Sucrose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Fructose
Maltose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Glucose
So, statement (ii) is true.
(iii) Polysaccharides are polymers of many monosaccharides and have no sweet taste.
So, statements (iii) is true.
(iv) Monosaccharides are categorised as reducing and non-reducing sugars.
So, statement (iv) is not true.

125006.subject: Botany
125006.text: Which component of ATP synthase contains the site for ATP synthesis?
125006.sol: This complex consists of two major components, F1 and F0 (Figure 12.5). The F1 headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F0 is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. The passage of protons through the channel is coupled to the catalytic site of the F1 component for the production of ATP. For each ATP produced, 4H+ passes through F0 from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient.

125451.subject: Botany
125451.text: Which enzyme is responsible for the fixation of CO2 in the mesophyll cells of C4 plants?
125451.sol: The pathway in C4 plants that has been named the Hatch and Slack Pathway, is again a cyclic process. The primary CO2 acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells. The enzyme responsible for this fixation is PEP carboxylase or PEPcase. It is important to register that the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO enzyme. The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells. It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells. In the bundle sheath cells these C4 acids are broken down to release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule. The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle.

125719.subject: Botany
125719.text: The photorespiratory carbon-oxidation cycle involves the interaction of
125719.sol: Photorespiration is a metabolic pathway that occurs in plants in the presence of light, in which ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase the (RuBisCO) enzyme involved in carbon dioxide fixation with ribulose bisphosphate, accepts oxygen, in place of carbon dioxide, resulting in the formation of a twocarbon compound, glycolate. Most of the fixed carbon represented by the glycolate can be salvaged by a series of reactions-the glycolate pathway - involving the peroxisomes and mitochondria, and returned to the chloroplasts. However, some of the carbon is lost as carbon dioxide. Unlike respiration there is no production of ATP.

125785.subject: Botany
125785.text: What should be made to elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers?
125785.sol: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca. 126210.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The egg apparatus is situated at the chalazal end of the embryo sac and consists of two synergids and one egg cell.

Reason (R): The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus, which play an important role in guiding the pollen tubes into the synergid.

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
126210.sol:
The egg apparatus is a 3-celled structure consisting of one egg cell and two synergids, but it is located at the micropylar end of the embryo sac, not the chalazal end. Three cells are grouped together at the chalazal end and are called the antipodals. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

The synergids possess special cellular thickenings at their micropylar tip known as the filiform apparatus. This structure plays a crucial role in guiding the pollen tubes into the synergid. Therefore, Reason (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

127932.subject: Zoology
127932.text: How do frogs respire in water?
127932.sol: Frogs respire on land and in the water by two different methods. In water, skin acts as aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as the respiratory organs. The respiration by lungs is called pulmonary respiration. The lungs are a pair of elongated, pink coloured sac-like structures present in the upper part of the trunk region (thorax). Air enters through the nostrils into the buccal cavity and then to lungs. During aestivation and hibernation gaseous exchange takes place through skin.

128102.subject: Zoology
128102.text:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) Some squamous or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion to form glandular epithelium.
(B) Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are examples of isolated glandular cells.
(C) Exocrine glands secrete their products directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
(D) Saliva, earwax and milk are secretions of exocrine glands.

How many of the above statements are correct?
128102.sol:
Let us evaluate each statement based on the NCERT description of glandular epithelium:

Statement (A) is incorrect. It is some of the columnar or cuboidal cells (not squamous) that get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium.

Statement (B) is correct. Unicellular glands consist of isolated glandular cells, and goblet cells of the alimentary canal are the classic example.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Exocrine glands release their products through ducts or tubes. It is the endocrine glands (which lack ducts) that secrete their products (hormones) directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

Statement (D) is correct. Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes, and other cell products.

Since statements (B) and (D) are correct, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

130582.subject: Zoology
130582.text: When should oral contraceptive pills ideally be started?
options: On the first day of the menstrual cycle
Within the first five days of the menstrual cycle
130582.sol: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by the females. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once a week’ pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

130752.subject: Zoology
130752.text: Which of the following pairs of diseases represents sexually transmitted infections that are completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
130752.sol:
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are diseases transmitted primarily through sexual intercourse.

According to NCERT, except for Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV infections, all other STIs (such as Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Chlamydiosis, Trichomoniasis, and Genital warts) are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

Genital herpes and Hepatitis-B are incurable STIs, making the options containing them incorrect. Malaria is a vector-borne disease, not an STI. Both Gonorrhoea and Chlamydiosis are STIs that are completely curable.

Answer: Gonorrhoea and Chlamydiosis

In fact, the presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience..

130904.text: What is the process by which the secondary oocyte (ovum) is released from the ovary?
130904.sol: The secondary oocyte retains bulk of the nutrient rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte. At present we are not very certain about this. The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle. The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it. The Graafian follicle now ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation
